q: The verifier raised findings on our emissions report. What do we do?
title: Responding to verifier findings
short: Read each finding, fix the cause rather than the symptom, and reply in writing with evidence. A misstatement means a number is wrong and must be corrected; a clarification request means the verifier needs more evidence. Findings left open, or material errors not corrected, can stop a clean statement.

ul: A factor from the wrong year.
Units mixed, such as kVAh treated as kWh.
Fuel bought counted instead of fuel used.

ol: Correct the figure and show the before and after.
Say what will stop it recurring.

sections.h: If a past year is affected
p: Restate it with a note, rather than carrying the error forward.

senseible: Senseible keeps every figure linked to its source invoice or bill with a fingerprint, so a verifier can trace a total back to the documents it came from.
